problem_statement: When the logging output includes the thread-id prefix (CONFIG_LOG_THREAD_ID_PREFIX) with the thread flag set, the prefix should show the emitting thread's priority alongside its name or address. For a named thread the prefix should look like "[ <prio> <name>] " (e.g. "[  5 main] "); when thread names are disabled the priority should still appear alongside the thread address ("[ <prio> 0x...] "). IRQ output (no thread) must remain "[irq] ".

problems.detail: The hidden tests require an exact 3-character-wide decimal priority format for both named-thread and address-thread output (the %3d field), but the statement only gives a generic placeholder and an example for the named case without specifying the width or exact spacing for the disabled-names case.

problem_statement_fixed: When the logging output includes the thread-id prefix (CONFIG_LOG_THREAD_ID_PREFIX) with the thread flag set, the prefix should show the emitting thread's priority alongside its name or address. The priority must be formatted as a 3-character-wide decimal field, for example a printf-style "%3d" field. For a named thread the prefix should look like "[ <prio> <name>] " (e.g. "[  5 main] "), where <prio> is the 3-wide decimal priority and <name> is the thread name. When thread names are disabled, the priority should still appear alongside the thread address in the form "[ <prio> 0x...] ", using the same 3-wide decimal priority and a pointer/address format for the thread address. IRQ output (no thread) must remain "[irq] ".
